topic: Harvest, Post-Harvest Handling, and Quality Standards

source.organization: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Cooperatives (MOALFC)
source.document: Potato Production Extension Resources & Post-Harvest Manuals

verification_sources.organization: Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Cooperatives (MOALFC)

document_summary: National extension framework guiding smallholders through maturity tracking indicators, manual dehaulming rules, skin curing steps, diffuse-light storage setups, and compliance with Kenyan crop packaging laws.
information_scope: Maturity indicators and strategic market harvesting timelines
Manual dehaulming, skin-setting mechanics, and harvesting weather rules
Post-harvest curing steps under high relative humidity
Diffuse-light storage architecture vs. dark ware potato storage
Compliance with national statutory agricultural packaging weights
common_farmer_observations: Freshly dug potatoes showing shredded or easily peeling skins when handled, leading to rapid storage rot.
Bags of potatoes tightly packed and extended far beyond standard limits, causing heavy crushing and bruising at the bottom.
Potatoes harvested mid-day under intense sunshine showing skin scorching and developing soft watery patches in storage.
Potatoes harvested prematurely during desperate cash-flow crunches, resulting in low dry-matter quality and poor shelf-life.
clarifying_questions: Did you allow the foliage to yellow and perform dehaulming ahead of harvest to give the skins time to fully set and harden inside the soil?
Are you storing your seed potatoes under cool diffused light to encourage greening, or are your eating potatoes exposed to light where they might turn green and toxic?
context_factors: Statutory packaging weight regulations in Kenya exist for scheduled crops to ensure standardized trading and protect handlers from carrying oversized, extended bags.
Curing harvested potatoes demands a short period under ambient room conditions with good air circulation and high humidity to heal field scratches.
Potato market dynamics are often highly seasonal, making post-harvest holding facilities vital to avoid selling at a loss during peak harvest gluts.
why_information_may_differ: Processing companies enforce strict grading metrics against surface scab or skin defects, while local fresh markets often tolerate moderate surface blemishes at standard pricing.
Industrial systems use chemical desiccants for dehaulming, whereas smallholders rely on clean, manual foliage slashing.
trusted_learning_points: Dehaulm the crop manually by cutting back the green canopy when leaves naturally yellow, leaving tubers underground for a short period to allow the outer skin to fully harden and set.
Harvest carefully during dry weather conditions, ideally during cool early mornings or late afternoons to avoid heat stress.
Allow dug tubers to briefly air-dry on the soil surface before collecting them into well-aerated transport crates or baskets.
Cure potatoes by keeping them in well-ventilated spaces with high humidity for a couple of weeks to allow physical field wounds to seal.
Store seed potatoes in Diffused Light Storage (DLS) structures to encourage short, tough green sprouts, but store ware potatoes in complete darkness to prevent greening.
Sort and grade tubers carefully using a seed gauge to remove all bruised, misshapen, or rotting pieces before transport.
Package crops according to official standardized weight regulations to avoid legal non-compliance and minimize internal handling damage.
possible_conflicting_information: Traditional practices favor immediate field bagging right after digging, but extension science shows that a brief drying period and dedicated curing step dramatically drop storage decay rates.
when_more_information_is_needed: When reviewing current statutory rules on crop trading, standardized bag weight limits, or local compliance checks.
When planning the construction of specialized diffused-light storage buildings using low-cost local timber and netting.
continue_learning: Engage with county sub-office extension staff to access local group marketing frameworks and training modules on post-harvest handling.
uncertainties: Unpredictable market price drops and shifting middleman dynamics that disrupt calculated storage and release timelines.
agronomic_principles: Skin setting is a physiological transformation triggered by canopy removal, rendering the tuber mechanically resilient.
Curing exploits the potato's natural healing ability, using humidity to form a protective layer over physical harvesting wounds.
Storage lighting serves as a biological switch: diffused light drives seed sprout development, while total darkness preserves ware quality.

knowledge_notes.focus: Help farmers understand principles rather than memorize procedures.
